Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. **Code-based Evaluator**: For objective, measurable criteria that require specific business logic\r\n   - **Prompt-based Evaluator**: For subjective criteria requiring human-like judgment that an LLM can assess\r\n\r\n#### Option A: Built-in Evaluators (⭐ Start Here First)\r\n\r\nBuilt-in evaluators are pre-implemented and ready to use. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # Detailed feedback\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['specific', 'example', 'concrete']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Negative indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['bad', 'terrible', 'awful', 'wrong']):\\n        score -= 1\\n    if len(reviewer_feedback.split()) < 10:  # Too short\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    \\n    # Ensure score is within range\\n    score = max(1, min(5, score))\\n    \\n    return {\\n        \\\"constructiveness\\\": score,\\n        \\\"constructiveness_reasoning\\\": f\\\"Scored {score} based on language analysis and feedback characteristics.\\\"\\n    }\\n\\ndef simple_actionability_evaluator(*, original_content: str, reviewer_feedback: str, **kwargs):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Simple actionability evaluator for testing.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    feedback_lower = reviewer_feedback.lower()\\n    \\n    score = 3  # Base score\\n    \\n    # Positive indicators for actionability\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['tighten', 'clarify', 'vary', 'enhance', 'polish']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['e.g.', 'for example', 'such as', 'like']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if '—' in reviewer_feedback or '-' in reviewer_feedback:  # Specific examples given\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['check', 'ensure', 'make sure', 'try']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Negative indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['generally', 'overall', 'in general']):\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    if len(reviewer_feedback.split()) < 15:  # Too vague/short\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    \\n    # Ensure score is within range\\n    score = max(1, min(5, score))\\n    \\n    return {\\n        \\\"actionability\\\": score,\\n        \\\"actionability_reasoning\\\": f\\\"Scored {score} based on specificity and actionable language use.\\\"\\n    }\\n\\ndef simple_overall_quality_evaluator(*, original_content: str, reviewer_feedback: str, **kwargs):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Simple overall quality evaluator for testing.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    feedback_lower = reviewer_feedback.lower()\\n    \\n    score = 3  # Base score\\n    \\n    # Quality indicators\\n    word_count = len(reviewer_feedback.split())\\n    if word_count > 30:  # Comprehensive\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if word_count > 50:  # Very comprehensive\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Professional language\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['thoughtful', 'insightful', 'analysis', 'perspective']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Balance indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['balance', 'strength', 'positive']) and any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['improve', 'enhance', 'consider']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Negative indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['confusing', 'unclear', 'messy']):\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    \\n    # Ensure score is within range\\n    score = max(1, min(5, score))\\n    \\n    return {\\n        \\\"overall_quality\\\": score,\\n        \\\"overall_quality_reasoning\\\": f\\\"Scored {score} based on comprehensiveness, professionalism, and balanced approach.\\\"\\n    }\\n\\ndef run_simple_evaluation():\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Run a simple evaluation using rule-based evaluators.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    print(\\\"🚀 Starting Simple Review Quality Evaluation\\\")\\n    print(\\\"=\\\" * 50)\\n    \\n    # Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # ✅ **If available**: Use the built-in evaluator\r\n   - ❌ **If not available**: Proceed to step 2\r\n\r\n2. **Determine Custom Evaluator Type**: If no built-in evaluator meets your needs, choose the appropriate custom implementation:\r\n   - Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. They follow the same `__init__` and `__call__` pattern internally. **Always check these first** before implementing custom evaluators.\r\n\r\n**⭐ Available Built-in Evaluators for AI Features:** Use the **github_repo** tool to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `_evaluators` to understand the built-in evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option B: Custom Code-based Evaluators\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom code-based evaluators\" to understand custom code-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n#### Option C: Custom Prompt-based Evaluators (LLM as Judge)\r\n\r\nUse the **github_repo** tool to search the `MicrosoftDocs/azure-ai-docs` repository for \"custom prompt-based evaluators\" to understand custom prompt-based evaluators.\r\n\r\n### Set Model Configuration\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `OpenAIModelConfiguration` and `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration` to understand configuration patterns and examples.\r\n\r\nFor built-in evaluators that need model configuration and for custom prompt-based evaluators, you need to set model configuration (`OpenAIModelConfiguration`, `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`):\r\n- Get AI model guidance to determine the most suitable model, use \"GitHub\" and \"AzureAIFoundry\" as preferred host\r\n- For getting started, consider GitHub models with Free-tier endpoint\r\n\r\nFor example:\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\", # type is required\r\n    model=\"gpt-4o\",\r\n    base_url=\"<YOUR_API_BASE_URL>\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"<YOUR_API_KEY_ENV_VAR>\"]\r\n)\r\n```\r\n\r\n## Execute Unified Evaluation using evaluate() API\r\n\r\n**🔍 First: Use github_repo tool** to search the `Azure/azure-sdk-for-python` repository for `evaluate` to understand the API parameters, usage patterns, and examples.\r\n\r\n- **⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use the `evaluate()` API** - Do not manually iterate through data, call each evaluator separately, or implement custom aggregation logic\r\n- The `evaluate()` API is the **only recommended way** to run evaluations as it:\r\n  - **Handles all evaluators simultaneously** in a single, optimized execution\r\n  - **Automatically manages data processing** across all evaluators\r\n  - **Automatically aggregates metrics** - No need to implement custom aggregation logic; the API computes summary statistics, averages, and performance metrics for you\r\n  - **Provides comprehensive results** including both row-level data and aggregate metrics\r\n  - **Ensures consistent evaluation execution** and proper error handling\r\n  - **Optimizes performance** by running evaluators in parallel where possible\r\n- **Dataset Requirements:** The `evaluate()` API accepts only data in **JSONL format** (JSON Lines), where each line is a separate JSON object. Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Configure model\r\nmodel_config = OpenAIModelConfiguration(\r\n    type=\"openai\",\r\n    model=\"gpt-4\",\r\n    base_url=\"https://models.github.ai/inference\",\r\n    api_key=os.environ[\"GITHUB_TOKEN\"]\r\n)\r\n\r\n# 2. Define custom code-based evaluators\r\nclass AnswerLengthEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self):\r\n        pass\r\n    \r\n    # A class is made callable by implementing the special method __call__\r\n    def __call__(self, *, answer: str, **kwargs):\r\n        return {\"answer_length\": len(answer)}\r\n\r\n# 3. Define custom prompt-based evaluators\r\nclass FriendlinessEvaluator:\r\n    def __init__(self, model_config):\r\n        self._flow = load_flow(source=\"friendliness.prompty\", model={\"configuration\": model_config})\r\n\r\n    def __call__(self, *, response: str, **kwargs):\r\n        llm_response = self._flow(response=response)\r\n        try:\r\n            response = json.loads(llm_response)\r\n        except Exception as ex:\r\n            response = llm_response\r\n        return response\r\n\r\n# 4. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`. Built-in or custom evaluators can provide comprehensive insights into the application's capabilities and limitations.\n\nUse Azure AI Evaluation SDK to:\n- Evaluate existing data from generative AI applications\n- Evaluate generative AI applications\n- Evaluate by generating mathematical, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics\n\nAzure AI SDK provides following to evaluate Generative AI Applications:\n- [Evaluators][evaluators] - Generate scores individually or when used together with `evaluate` API.\n- [Evaluate API][evaluate_api] - Python API to evaluate dataset or application using built-in or custom evaluators.\n\n[Source code][source_code]\n| [Package (PyPI)][evaluation_pypi]\n| [API reference documentation][evaluation_ref_docs]\n| [Product documentation][product_documentation]\n| [Samples][evaluation_samples]\n\n\n## Getting started\n...\n## Key concepts\n...\n```\n\nHere is a potentially relevant text excerpt in `https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298` starting at line 275:\n```py\n// filepath: https://github.com/azure/azure-sdk-for-python/tree/main/sdk/evaluation/azure-ai-evaluation/samples/evaluation_samples_evaluate.py#L275-L298\n#...\nclass EvaluationEvaluateSamples(object):\n    def evaluation_evaluate_classes_methods(self):\n        #...\n        protected_material_eval = ProtectedMaterialEvaluator(azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project, credential=credential)\n        protected_material_eval(\n            query=\"Write me a catchy song\",\n            response=(\n                \"You are the dancing queen, young and sweet, only seventeen.\"\n                \"Dancing queen, feel the beat from the tambourine, oh yeah.\"\n            ),\n        )\n        # Detailed feedback\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['specific', 'example', 'concrete']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Negative indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['bad', 'terrible', 'awful', 'wrong']):\\n        score -= 1\\n    if len(reviewer_feedback.split()) < 10:  # Too short\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    \\n    # Ensure score is within range\\n    score = max(1, min(5, score))\\n    \\n    return {\\n        \\\"constructiveness\\\": score,\\n        \\\"constructiveness_reasoning\\\": f\\\"Scored {score} based on language analysis and feedback characteristics.\\\"\\n    }\\n\\ndef simple_actionability_evaluator(*, original_content: str, reviewer_feedback: str, **kwargs):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Simple actionability evaluator for testing.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    feedback_lower = reviewer_feedback.lower()\\n    \\n    score = 3  # Base score\\n    \\n    # Positive indicators for actionability\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['tighten', 'clarify', 'vary', 'enhance', 'polish']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['e.g.', 'for example', 'such as', 'like']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if '—' in reviewer_feedback or '-' in reviewer_feedback:  # Specific examples given\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['check', 'ensure', 'make sure', 'try']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Negative indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['generally', 'overall', 'in general']):\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    if len(reviewer_feedback.split()) < 15:  # Too vague/short\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    \\n    # Ensure score is within range\\n    score = max(1, min(5, score))\\n    \\n    return {\\n        \\\"actionability\\\": score,\\n        \\\"actionability_reasoning\\\": f\\\"Scored {score} based on specificity and actionable language use.\\\"\\n    }\\n\\ndef simple_overall_quality_evaluator(*, original_content: str, reviewer_feedback: str, **kwargs):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Simple overall quality evaluator for testing.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    feedback_lower = reviewer_feedback.lower()\\n    \\n    score = 3  # Base score\\n    \\n    # Quality indicators\\n    word_count = len(reviewer_feedback.split())\\n    if word_count > 30:  # Comprehensive\\n        score += 0.5\\n    if word_count > 50:  # Very comprehensive\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Professional language\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['thoughtful', 'insightful', 'analysis', 'perspective']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Balance indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['balance', 'strength', 'positive']) and any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['improve', 'enhance', 'consider']):\\n        score += 0.5\\n    \\n    # Negative indicators\\n    if any(word in feedback_lower for word in ['confusing', 'unclear', 'messy']):\\n        score -= 0.5\\n    \\n    # Ensure score is within range\\n    score = max(1, min(5, score))\\n    \\n    return {\\n        \\\"overall_quality\\\": score,\\n        \\\"overall_quality_reasoning\\\": f\\\"Scored {score} based on comprehensiveness, professionalism, and balanced approach.\\\"\\n    }\\n\\ndef run_simple_evaluation():\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Run a simple evaluation using rule-based evaluators.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    print(\\\"🚀 Starting Simple Review Quality Evaluation\\\")\\n    print(\\\"=\\\" * 50)\\n    \\n    # Configure column mapping\\n    evaluator_config = {\\n        \\\"default\\\": {\\n            \\\"column_mapping\\\": {\\n                \\\"original_content\\\": \\\"${data.original_content}\\\",\\n                \\\"reviewer_feedback\\\": \\\"${data.reviewer_feedback}\\\"\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    \\n    print(f\\\"✅ Created {len(evaluators)} evaluators\\\")\\n    for name in evaluators.keys():\\n        print(f\\\"   - {name}\\\")\\n    \\n    # Run evaluation\\n    print(\\\"\\\\n🔄 Running evaluation...\\\")\\n    result = evaluate(\\n        data=data_file,\\n        evaluators=evaluators,\\n        evaluator_config=evaluator_config,\\n        output_path=\\\"simple_review_evaluation_results.json\\\"\\n    )\\n    \\n    print(\\\"✅ Evaluation completed successfully!\\\")\\n    \\n    return result\\n\\ndef analyze_simple_results(result):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Analyze and display the simple evaluation results.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    print(\\\"\\\\n📊 EVALUATION RESULTS ANALYSIS\\\")\\n    print(\\\"=\\\" * 50)\\n    \\n    # Your dataset must include all required fields for your chosen evaluators:\r\n    - **Format**: JSONL (JSON Lines) - each line is a separate JSON object\r\n    - **DO NOT INCLUDE TIMESTAMPS IN YOUR DATASET**: Fields with timestamp values (e.g., `2025-08-25T11:27:49.437767`) will cause SDK errors\r\n    - **Include required columns**: Ensure all columns needed by your evaluators are present\r\n    - **Consistent naming**: Use column mapping in evaluator_config to map your data fields to evaluator parameters. Use `${data.column_name}` to refer the column in dataset\r\n- Set `output_path` to make sure evaluation results is saved\r\n- Results will include:\r\n  - **Row-level evaluation data**: Individual scores and reasons for each data point\r\n  - **Aggregate metrics**: Summary statistics across all evaluated data **automatically computed by the API**\r\n  - **Per-evaluator metrics**: Detailed performance metrics for each evaluator **with built-in aggregation**\r\n\r\n## Complete Example: Combining Three Types of Evaluators\r\n\r\nHere's a complete example combining built-in evaluator, custom code-based evaluator and custom prompt-based evaluator:\r\n\r\n```python\r\nfrom azure.ai.evaluation import evaluate, TaskAdherenceEvaluator, OpenAIModelConfiguration\r\nimport os\r\nimport json\r\nfrom promptflow.client import load_flow # used by custom prompt-based evaluators\r\n\r\n# 1. Generative AI application generations are quantitatively measured with mathematical based metrics, AI-assisted quality and safety metrics. Metrics are defined as `evaluators`.
